cards.front: squash
cards.back: To press something so it gets flatter. A sponge can squash.
cards.say: squash. To press something so it gets flatter. A sponge can squash.

cards.front: bend
cards.back: To change a shape so that it is curved. A wire can bend.
cards.say: bend. To change a shape so that it is curved. A wire can bend.

cards.front: twist
cards.back: To turn the two ends of something in opposite directions. You can twist a towel.
cards.say: twist. To turn the two ends of something in opposite directions. You can twist a towel.

cards.front: stretch
cards.back: To pull something so it gets longer. A rubber band can stretch.
cards.say: stretch. To pull something so it gets longer. A rubber band can stretch.

cards.front: melt
cards.back: To change from solid to liquid when heated. Ice melts.
cards.say: melt. To change from solid to liquid when heated. Ice melts.

cards.front: freeze
cards.back: To change from liquid to solid when cooled. Water freezes into ice.
cards.say: freeze. To change from liquid to solid when cooled. Water freezes into ice.

cards.front: What happens to ice when it is heated?
cards.say: What happens to ice when it is heated? It melts into water.

cards.front: What happens to water when it is cooled a lot?
cards.say: What happens to water when it is cooled a lot? It freezes into ice.

cards.front: What happens to chocolate in the Sun?
cards.say: What happens to chocolate in the Sun? It melts.

cards.front: What happens to a sponge when you squash it?
cards.back: It gets flatter. It goes back when you let go.
cards.say: What happens to a sponge when you squash it? It gets flatter. It goes back when you let go.

cards.front: What happens to a clay ball when you squash it?
cards.back: It stays flat. Clay keeps its new shape.
cards.say: What happens to a clay ball when you squash it? It stays flat. Clay keeps its new shape.

cards.front: Which can you stretch: a rubber band or a pencil?
cards.say: Which can you stretch: a rubber band or a pencil? A rubber band.

cards.front: Which can you bend: a wire or a stone?
cards.say: Which can you bend: a wire or a stone? A wire.

cards.front: Which can you twist: a towel or a plate?
cards.say: Which can you twist: a towel or a plate? A towel.

cards.front: What happens to a candle when it is heated?
cards.say: What happens to a candle when it is heated? The wax melts.

cards.front: What happens to butter in a hot pan?
cards.say: What happens to butter in a hot pan? It melts.

cards.front: What happens to an ice lolly on a hot day?
cards.say: What happens to an ice lolly on a hot day? It melts.

cards.front: What happens to puddles when it is very cold?
cards.say: What happens to puddles when it is very cold? They can freeze.

cards.front: What happens to a wet cloth in the Sun?
cards.say: What happens to a wet cloth in the Sun? It dries.

cards.front: Is melting a change you can reverse?
cards.back: Yes, for ice. Cool the water and it freezes again.
cards.say: Is melting a change you can reverse? Yes, for ice. Cool the water and it freezes again.

cards.front: Is cooking an egg a change you can reverse?
cards.back: No. A cooked egg cannot become raw again.
cards.say: Is cooking an egg a change you can reverse? No. A cooked egg cannot become raw again.

cards.front: What happens to a balloon when you blow into it?
cards.say: What happens to a balloon when you blow into it? It stretches and gets bigger.
